comments.text:
Fun fact: China actually has its own “Great Green Wall.” 😂

The Mu Us Sandy Land in northern China used to have huge areas of shifting sand dunes, partly due to centuries of vegetation loss, overgrazing and desertification. Since the 1950s, massive restoration projects have been carried out there, using grasses, shrubs, shelterbelts and other methods to stabilize the sand.

Today, over 90% of the desertified land in the Yulin area has been brought under control, and large areas that were once shifting dunes are now covered by grassland, shrubs, farmland and sparse forests.

It’s sometimes reported as “China made a desert disappear,” which isn’t quite accurate — the sand is still there. What disappeared, for the most part, are the moving dunes. The goal was basically to stop the sand from moving and allow vegetation to return.

So yeah… the Great Wall stopped people, and the Great Green Wall stops sand. 😂🌱
